title: SystemDesignReview
description: A grounded, evolve-under-load system-design review of one flow. The flow is broken into 2-5 VERSIONS, each an incremental architecture that fixes the previous version's failure and (usually) introduces the next problem. Each version has a positioned node/edge/group graph. The renderer (template.html) consumes this object directly as REVIEW.

review_title.description: Short human title for the flow under review, e.g. 'Mobile sign-up flow' or 'Video upload + commit'.

summary.description: 1-2 sentence plain-language description of the flow and what this review evolves it toward.

target_scale.description: The scale this review is calibrated to. Default posture is 'next 10x' from where the app is today. State concrete numbers, e.g. 'Next 10x: ~50k DAU, ~2k signups/day, ~800 video uploads/day'.

grounding.description: Where this flow lives in the real codebase. Every claim about the CURRENT state must trace to real files you opened.

current_version.description: Which version id ('you are here') most closely matches what the code does TODAY.

notes.description: 1-3 sentences on how the current code maps to version 1, with file:line citations.

systems.description: Distinct systems/layers this review touches, in first-appearance order. Drives the legend. Each must be a key in the SYSTEMS registry in template.html.

versions.description: The ordered versions. DO NOT pad to 4: use exactly as many as the flow needs (2-5). Each version fixes the previous one's `breaks` and usually introduces a `new_problem`.

name.description: Short version name, e.g. 'Naive synchronous', 'Add a queue', 'Transactional outbox'.

tagline.description: <=6 word subtitle shown under the version name, e.g. 'Everything in the request'.

adds.description: 2-4 sentences: what this version introduces vs the previous one, and why. Plain language.

breaks.description: Where this version fails AND the concrete scale/condition that triggers it, e.g. 'Email provider slow (~2s) or down blocks the request; at ~300 concurrent signups every API worker is tied up'. Omit only for the final, terminal version if it has no material failure at target scale.

new_problem.description: Optional. The new problem this fix introduces, which the next version solves. Omit on the final version.

verdict.description: The stack recommendation for THIS version, calibrated to target_scale. This is what makes the review actionable and anti-over-engineering.

status.description: here-today = closest to current code; adopt-now = worth doing before target scale; defer = don't build until a stated threshold; target = the recommended end state for target_scale.

note.description: 1-2 sentences justifying the status, grounded in the stack ledger, e.g. 'Do this with a Postgres outbox table + the existing cron worker; you do NOT need SQS until >X jobs/min.'

nodes.description: Components in this version's architecture, positioned on a grid.

id.description: Stable id, unique within the version. Reuse the SAME id across versions for a component that persists (keeps it in place when toggling).

system.description: Key in the SYSTEMS registry (drives color + icon).

x.description: Grid column (fractional allowed). Columns typically 0,1,2,3. Same component should keep the same x/y across versions.

y.description: Grid row (fractional allowed), increasing downward. Entry point at top.

status.description: Optional. 'new' = introduced in this version (gets a glow + NEW badge); 'changed' = same node, new behavior.

note.description: Optional. 1-3 sentences shown when the node is clicked: what it does and any real file:line if it maps to Meels code.

edges.description: Directed connections between nodes in this version.

label.description: Optional short label on the edge, e.g. 'submit', 'enqueue', 'after 5 fails'.

kind.description: sync=blocking gray; async=non-blocking blue (marching-ants); write=purple; read=cyan; fail=red dashed (e.g. -> DLQ). Default sync.

groups.description: Optional dashed bounding boxes around related nodes, e.g. a transactional boundary or a deployment region.

kind.description: Drives the box accent color. Default boundary.
